This iconic dish offers a perfect balance of sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy flavors, making it a comforting and luxurious meal. Prepare to impress your taste buds with this rich and aromatic culinary masterpiece.

instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 teaspoon red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala, 1 teaspoon salt, and lemon juice. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and saute until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Sauce
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree, 1 teaspoon red chili powder, and 1 teaspoon garam masala. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil starts to separate from the edges.

instructions.title: Blend for Creaminess
instructions.text: Drain the soaked cashews and add them to the sauce. Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender. Blend until completely smooth. Pass the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture, if desired.

instructions.title: Finish the Butter Chicken
instructions.text: Return the smooth sauce to the pan over low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces, water or broth, honey or sugar, and crushed kasuri methi. Stir well and simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the sauce.

instructions.title: Add Cream and Garnish
instructions.text: Stir in the heavy cream. Cook for just 1-2 minutes more, ensuring the sauce does not boil vigorously after adding cream. Taste and adjust salt and sweetness if needed. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro and a swirl of extra cream before serving.

article:
Indian cuisine offers a kaleidoscope of flavors, aromas, and textures, making it a beloved choice for any meal, especially a satisfying lunch. Among its vast repertoire, one dish stands out as a global superstar: Butter Chicken, known in India as Murgh Makhani. This iconic curry, with its velvety texture, rich tomato-based gravy, and tender pieces of chicken, has captivated palates worldwide. It’s the ultimate comfort food, perfectly balanced with mild spices and a luxurious creaminess that makes it an irresistible Indian lunch recipe. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home, you're in the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to master this culinary masterpiece.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Its origins trace back to the 1950s in Delhi, at the Moti Mahal restaurant, where it was supposedly created by Kundan Lal Jaggi. The story goes that leftover tandoor-cooked chicken was simmered in a rich tomato and butter-based gravy to prevent it from drying out. The result was a culinary revelation that quickly gained popularity.

What defines authentic Murgh Makhani is its distinctive flavor profile: a harmonious blend of tangy tomatoes, aromatic spices, and the unmistakable richness of butter and cream. The chicken is typically marinated in yogurt and spices, then traditionally cooked in a tandoor (clay oven) or pan-fried until slightly charred, imparting a subtle smokiness. This cooked chicken is then introduced to a luscious, often strained, gravy, ensuring a smooth and luxurious texture. Unlike many other Indian curries, Butter Chicken is relatively mild, making it approachable for those new to Indian cuisine, while still offering a depth of flavor that keeps connoisseurs coming back for more. It's truly a dish that embodies indulgence and comfort, making it a perfect centerpiece for an Indian lunch.

## Ingredients for Authentic Butter Chicken

Creating the perfect Butter Chicken requires a few key components, divided into the chicken marinade and the rich gravy.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri for color)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp garam masala
*   1/2 tsp salt
*   1 tbsp lemon juice

**For the Makhani Gravy:**
*   2 tbsp unsalted butter (plus more for finishing)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped (optional, for extra body)
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes or 3-4 large ripe tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes, then drained)
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri)
*   1 tsp ground coriander
*   1/2 tsp ground cumin
*   1/4 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1-2 tbsp sugar (to balance acidity)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (plus more for garnish)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Butter Chicken

Follow these steps to create a show-stopping Butter Chicken that will impress even the most discerning palates.

**Step 1: Marinate the Chicken**
In a large bowl, combine all the ingredients for the chicken marinade. Add the chicken pieces and toss to coat evenly. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for best results.

**Step 2: Cook the Chicken**
Heat a tablespoon of oil or butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear the chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until it's cooked through and has a slight char. Remove the cooked chicken and set it aside.

**Step 3: Prepare the Gravy Base**
In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. If using, add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in the pureed tomatoes, soaked cashews, Kashmiri chili powder, ground coriander, ground cumin, and turmeric powder. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have softened and the oil starts to separate from the mixture.

**Step 4: Blend and Strain the Gravy**
Remove the pan from heat and let the mixture cool slightly. Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender. Add 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth and blend until completely smooth. For an ultra-silky, restaurant-style gravy, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot, pressing down on any solids to extract all the liquid. Discard the remaining pulp.

**Step 5: Simmer the Gravy**
Return the strained gravy to the pot and place it over medium-low heat. Bring it to a gentle simmer.

**Step 6: Combine and Finish**
Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir in the kasoori methi (crushed between your palms to release its aroma), the remaining butter (start with 1-2 tablespoons and add more to taste), and the sugar. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to warm through. Finally, stir in the heavy cream. Do not boil vigorously after adding cream. Taste and adjust salt as needed.

**Step 7: Garnish and Serve**
Garnish your homemade Butter Chicken generously with fresh chopped cilantro and a swirl of extra cream, if desired.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving that authentic, mouth-watering Butter Chicken flavor is easier with these expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't rush the marination process. Longer marination (4+ hours) ensures tender, flavorful chicken that truly absorbs the spices.
*   **Kashmiri Chili Powder:** This specific chili powder provides a beautiful, vibrant red color to the gravy without adding excessive heat. It's crucial for the aesthetic appeal of Butter Chicken.
*   **Kasoori Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves):** This ingredient is non-negotiable! It adds a unique, slightly bitter, and earthy aroma that is signature to Murgh Makhani. Lightly toast the leaves in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing them to intensify their flavor.
*   **Smooth Gravy:** Blending the gravy base until perfectly smooth and then straining it is the secret to that luxurious, silky texture found in high-end Indian restaurants. Don't skip this step if you want the best results.
*   **Don't Skimp on Butter and Cream:** These are defining ingredients. While you can adjust slightly for dietary reasons, authentic Butter Chicken embraces its richness.
*   **Balance Sweet and Tangy:** The sugar helps balance the acidity of the tomatoes. Taste and adjust to achieve your preferred sweet-tangy equilibrium.
*   **Chicken Thighs vs. Breast:** Boneless, skinless chicken thighs are generally recommended as they stay more tender and flavorful than chicken breast, which can dry out quickly.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments, making it an ideal choice for a hearty Indian lunch.

The classic pairing is with **Naan bread** or **Roti**, perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich, creamy gravy. Alternatively, serve it alongside fragrant **Basmati rice**, plain or as Jeera Rice (cumin rice), allowing the rice to soak up the luxurious sauce. For a complete meal, add a simple side salad of sliced cucumbers and onions, or a cooling raita (yogurt dip) to balance the richness. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice over the top just before serving can also brighten the flavors.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect as is, there are several ways to adapt it to dietary needs or personal preferences:

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Substitute the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese) to make **Paneer Makhani**, or use firm tofu, mushrooms, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower and peas for a delicious vegetarian version.
*   **Vegan Butter Chicken:** Replace dairy yogurt with a plant-based alternative, use olive oil or vegan butter, and substitute heavy cream with full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream for a rich, dairy-free gravy.
*   **Spice Level:** If you prefer more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili to the gravy base. For less heat, reduce the chili powder.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** If you don't have a grill or tandoor, you can impart a smoky flavor by using the "dhungar" method. Place a small piece of burning charcoal in a small heat-proof bowl within the pot of finished curry, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over it, and cover immediately for a few minutes.
*   **Healthier Options:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream slightly, or use low-fat versions. You can also increase the vegetable content in the gravy by adding pureed carrots or bell peppers for extra nutrients.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What's the difference between Butter Chicken and Chicken Tikka Masala?**
A: While both are popular creamy, tomato-based chicken curries, they have distinct differences. Butter Chicken is generally milder, sweeter, and focuses heavily on butter and cream, with a subtle tang from tomatoes. Chicken Tikka Masala, on the other hand, often features a more complex blend of spices, can be spicier, and its gravy might have a slightly coarser texture and a more pronounced onion-tomato base, sometimes with yogurt. The chicken in Tikka Masala is always "tikka" (marinated and grilled/tandoor-cooked).

**Q: Can I make Butter Chicken ahead of time?**
A: Absolutely! Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld and deepen. You can prepare the entire dish and store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3-4 days. It also freezes well for up to 3 months; thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the stovetop.

**Q: Is Butter Chicken spicy?**
A: Traditionally, Butter Chicken is not meant to be spicy. It's known for its mild, rich, and creamy profile. The heat comes primarily from red chili powder, which is often Kashmiri chili powder, used more for color than intense spice. However, you can easily adjust the spice level to your preference by adding more or less chili powder or fresh green chilies.

**Q: What kind of chicken is best for Butter Chicken?**
A: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs are highly recommended for Butter Chicken. They remain incredibly tender and juicy even after cooking, absorbing the flavors beautifully. Chicken breast can be used, but it has a tendency to dry out if overcooked. If using breast, ensure it's cut into uniform pieces and not overcooked during the searing stage.

Mastering Butter Chicken at home is a rewarding culinary journey. With this comprehensive guide, you're well-equipped to create a truly authentic and delicious Murgh Makhani that will become a cherished Indian lunch recipe in your home. Enjoy the rich, comforting flavors of this timeless classic!
